title: Allergic rhinitis symptoms, 28-year-old woman (saved regression case 2)
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Sneezing, runny and itchy nose with nasal blockage for 3 weeks, worse in the mornings.
intake.history: No fever. Similar episodes every year.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 5. A: All vital signs are normal, afebrile, pain 0. Adult vitals p7: 'Vital Signs within normal limits' is printed in BOTH the Level 4 (x~358) and Level 5 (x~453) columns; 'No Fever', 'No Pain' are Level 5 (x~453). Complaint list: EAR/ENT p9 'All other presentations' is Level 5 (x~453); RESPIRATORY p10 'Mild URTI symptoms' is Level 5 (x~453). The complaint list separates L4 from L5, so Level 5. Level 4 is defensible under the 'higher modifier' rule because the normal-vitals cell sits in both columns. MTS p6 also allows triage-away to outpatient services for non-urgent presentations with normal vital signs. B: The Ear/ENT complaint row gives Level 5 'All other presentations' (p9, x~453). Respiratory 'Mild URTI symptoms' is Level 5 (p10, x~453). Vital signs, afebrile and no pain are all Level 5 (p7, x~453). But the adult vital-signs table prints 'Vital Signs within normal limits' in both the Level 4 (x~358) and Level 5 (x~453) columns. A literal reading of the 'higher level modifier when modifiers do not differentiate' rule (p7) would give Level 4, so 4 is in 'acceptable'. The quotes 'All other presentations' also appear in the Eye row on p9; the ENT row is the relevant one.

disposition.note: Stable, normal vital signs, no red flags: discharge with treatment and primary-care follow-up. ORL/allergy referral only if symptoms stay uncontrolled on pharmacotherapy, or if a referral criterion from the rhinosinusitis CPG appears (none is present). Check the ETD redirection policy: triage-away is permitted by MTS for non-urgent cases, but the Selangor redirection clauses may restrict sending patients away. / Normal vital signs and a chronic non-urgent complaint: discharge with treatment and follow-up at a primary care clinic (KK). Refer to ORL or allergy only if symptoms stay uncontrolled or red flags appear.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: The corpus has no dedicated KKM allergic-rhinitis CPG (no ARIA-type guideline). Treatment items rely on the Asthma in Adults CPG 2024 comorbidity section, the Rhinosinusitis CPG 2016 (antihistamine recommendation, differential table, INCS formulary) and the MSAI SLIT consensus 2023 (a society statement, not MOH).

Antibiotics: no source explicitly forbids them for allergic rhinitis. The Rhinosinusitis CPG reserves antibiotics for severe acute bacterial rhinosinusitis. Not listed as forbidden; the adjudicator may want an 'antibiotics not indicated' check.
Level 4 vs 5: the adult vitals table prints 'Vital Signs within normal limits' under both Level 4 and Level 5.
B: No KKM CPG is written for allergic rhinitis itself. The evidence is borrowed from the Rhinosinusitis CPG (differential table, Recommendation 7, Appendix 5 drug table) and the MSAI SLIT consensus.
Triage 4 vs 5 depends on how the 'Vital Signs within normal limits' cell, printed in both the L4 and L5 columns, combines with the 'higher level' rule.
The forbidden decongestant item concerns duration only (topical decongestant > 2 weeks). A short course is not forbidden, so its matcher is deliberately narrow and required=false.
If the ED is in Selangor, the JKN Selangor redirection policy may limit triaging her away; this was not checked for this case.
